_comment: 🔮️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform: the `image` 0.25 reference codec registered specifically for JFIF 1.01 mutation coverage (distinct from the shared `image-jpeg` entry's `jpg-raster` capability), the exhaustive JpgMutation vocabulary it is measured against, and the coarse-tolerance comparison profile a lossy round trip through two independently written codecs needs.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED. The third-party crate here does REAL codec work — it decodes the artifact and will reject a malformed one — but that is not what the mutation test turns on. What the OUTPUT OF A MUTATION SHOULD BE is computed by this owner's own `🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs`, whose `apply_kind` dispatch is a second implementation of this subset's mutation semantics. Its own doc comment says so: it "deliberately mirrors" the production `diff` rather than diverging from it. Both halves of the comparison therefore read the same specification, and a misreading of it produces two agreeing wrong answers.

The honest split is that the crate discharges "the result is a well-formed file of this format", and NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for, so this is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed.

productionDebt.plan: Same underlying `image` crate reachability already recorded against the shared `image-jpeg` entry (✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️.json) — repeated here because the dependency gate keys recorded debt by (path, oracle id) pair, not by package, so a second oracle id sharing the same package needs its own record. Phase 7 target: both call sites want raster decode/encode that ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio already implements, so routing them through decode_bmp / decode_tiff / decode_jpg retires the dependency and every entry recording it, this one included.

Same package, same reachability finding as the sibling `image-jpeg-jfif-1-01-mutate` entry immediately above — repeated here because the dependency gate keys recorded debt by (path, oracle id) pair. Independently re-verified this session by reading the source at both `reachableFrom` paths directly: `writer` module in the animate video component (`use image::{ImageBuffer, Rgba};`, a real non-test partial-movie-writer path) and `upload_tile` in the surface tiled-map component (`image::load_from_memory`, a real non-test production method) — both non-optional, non-dev `image` dependencies per their own Cargo.toml. The repository-wide `🔒️dependencies.json` registry entry for `image` currently still reads `productionReachable: false`, which this finding contradicts; that shared file is not edited here (out of this ticket's scope), only this oracle's own field is corrected to match the evidence.

oracles.rationale:
📖️ A READER, and that is the whole point of registering it separately from the `cross-semio-implementation` entry immediately above.

That sibling entry carries a `🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs` that COMPUTES what each mutation should produce — registered `cross-semio-implementation` precisely because it shares one reading of the spec with production. This entry is a different mechanism entirely: the expected state is not computed at all, it is COMMITTED, as the `after` half of a byte-reproducible fixture built directly by `../🏭️generator/🦀️jpeg-jfif-codec` (depends on nothing but `image` 0.25.10). `image`'s own decoder then reads BOTH sides and the comparison is over what it recovered. The probes say so in their own header: "Everything here MARSHALS and READS; nothing here applies a mutation or predicts what one should."

CHECKED AGAINST THE VENDORED CRATE SOURCE, not assumed (`~/.cargo/registry/src/…/image-0.25.10` and `zune-jpeg-0.5.15`): `image::codecs::jpeg::JpegDecoder`'s public `ImageDecoder` surface exposes only `dimensions`, `color_type`, `icc_profile`, `exif_metadata`, `xmp_metadata`, `iptc_metadata`, `orientation` and the decoded raster — no DQT/DHT/DRI accessor exists anywhere in either crate, and `zune_jpeg::decoder::ImageInfo`'s `x_density`/`y_density` fields (documented "Found in the APP(0) marker") are dead: their setters are never called anywhere in the crate, so they always read back zero regardless of the file's real JFIF header. This governs the split registered on this subset's ten mutation kinds below: four are witnessable through this reader (`insert-other-segment`/`remove-other-segment`, built with an APP1 XMP payload specifically — the one generic-segment shape `xmp_metadata()` actually surfaces; `replace-pixels` and `change-re-encode-quality`, witnessed through the decoded raster digest) and six carry `jpg-jfif-1-01-mutate-uncarried` instead: five (`replace-quant-table`, `remove-quant-table`, `replace-huffman-table`, `remove-huffman-table`, `change-restart-interval`) because this subset's OWN production encoder (`../../🚪️io/🦀️component.rs::encode_jpg`) provably never carries them into the bytes at all — it regenerates fresh Annex K DQT/DHT tables from `re_encode_quality` on every write and never emits a DRI marker, independently confirmed by reading that file directly, not merely quoted from the sibling oracle's own docstring — and `change-jfif-header` because although `image`'s OWN encoder can write a genuine density difference (`set_pixel_density`, a real public API, used to build this kind's own fixture), this reader has no decode-side way to read it back.

MEASURED, and this is what qualifies the registration rather than merely motivating it: `jpg-compare` on a byte-identical pair (`insert-other-segment-applied/before.jpg` against itself) returns `equal:true, diffCount:0`; on the real before/after pair for the same recipe (a genuine spliced APP1 XMP segment) it returns `equal:false, diffCount:3`, naming `$.xmp.present`, `$.xmp.size` and `$.xmp.digest` exactly.

engine.implementation: Pillow 11.3.0 JPEG marker reader (quantization tables, JFIF APP0)

oracles.rationale:
📖️ A SECOND reader for this subset, on facts the first one destroys on its way to pixels.

`image`-rs DECODES a JPEG: the quantisation tables and the JFIF APP0 segment are consumed and discarded, so no projection built on it can witness them. That is why six kinds were recorded `-uncarried` against it — honest about `image`, and not a claim about JPEG readers generally.

Pillow keeps both — `im.quantization` and `im.info['jfif_version'|'jfif_unit'|'jfif_density']` — and can also WRITE the differences: a different `quality` produces different quantisation tables, and `dpi=` rewrites the JFIF density and unit. Writer and reader being one library matches the precedent already accepted here (gif's Encoder writes, its Decoder judges).

MEASURED before registering, and the measurement set the scope: `replace-quant-table` and `change-jfif-header` each move this projection. `change-restart-interval` does NOT — Pillow does not read the DRI segment back — and the Huffman accessors return empty and are deprecated for removal in Pillow 12, so `replace-huffman-table` and `remove-huffman-table` cannot be witnessed either. Those three stay `-uncarried` rather than being claimed.

🔍️`remove-quant-table` was ONCE in that list, on the reasoning that a JPEG without a quantisation table is not a decodable JPEG. That is true and was the wrong question: the kind removes a table from the TABLE LIST, and a JPEG may legally have its components share ONE table instead of two. Pillow's `qtables=` writes exactly that — `[STD, STD]` produces two tables and `[STD]` produces one, at the same mode and size — so the table COUNT moves and nothing else does. Measured: ['0','1'] -> ['0'], mode RGB on both sides. The kind is carried.

engine.implementation: djpeg -v -v marker dump; jpegtran lossless transcode

oracles.rationale:
📖️ A third-party CLI, and the first in this subset — Protocol v2 lists `third-party-cli` alongside `third-party-library` as a qualifying kind, and this is where that clause earns its place.

These two kinds were recorded uncarried after every available LIBRARY was checked, and that survey was correct as far as it went: `image`-rs decodes to pixels; Pillow's DRI handler is literally `Skip` and its Huffman accessors return empty and are deprecated for removal in Pillow 12; `zune-jpeg` 0.5.15 parses the DRI marker but keeps `restart_interval` `pub(crate)` (`decoder.rs:144`). What the survey never covered is that the INVENTORY ITSELF was scoped to libraries — cargo, npm and PyPI — and never to installed command-line tools.

`djpeg -v -v` prints every marker libjpeg walks: quantisation tables with their values, Huffman tables with their code-length counts, the Start-of-Frame, and `Define Restart Interval N`. Measured: a `-restart` transcode moves the projection from `restartInterval: null` to `4`, and an `-optimize` transcode changes the Huffman code-length rows (`0 1 5 1 1 1...` becomes `1 1 1 0 0 0...`).

The WRITER is `jpegtran` from the same toolchain, and it is a LOSSLESS transcoder: `-restart` and `-optimize` re-emit the identical image, so each pair differs in its marker structure and in nothing else. The generator asserts the Start-of-Frame line is unchanged rather than trusting the documentation.

The banner lines are dropped from the projection: they carry the tool's build date, which would otherwise make the same fixture project differently on two machines.

comparisonProfiles.description: JFIF 1.01 JPEG mutation round trips. The LOSSY half — `lumaHistogram`, an 8-bucket luma census — is the only numeric member, and the only one the tolerance below is for: the reference `image` codec and this subset's own from-scratch codec are two independently written implementations, so a real photographic fixture re-encoded through each lands luma mass in the same coarse buckets but not identical per-bucket counts. Raw samples are never reported: this platform's comparison tolerance is per-number and absolute with no aggregate mode, so an unbounded sample array could never be compared honestly. Every EXACT member — `dimensions`, `jfifVersion`, `jfifDensity`, each retained segment's marker/length/payload digest, and each DQT payload digest — is spelled as a STRING on purpose, because the comparison engine applies `tolerance` to numbers and compares strings by equality: reported as numbers under a 400000 slack, the real 2275x2560 scan and a 3x2 stub compared EQUAL, and so did every JFIF header field. The slack is sized against the ~5.8 megapixel real-world fixture this case reads (shared://🖼️abbau-aufbau-masterarbeit-grundriss.jpg): measured, one decode/re-encode at quality 90 moves at most 2018 pixels between buckets, a pass through quality 50 at most 10014 and through quality 5 at most 55570 — so it still fails genuine corruption (blank, inverted or solid output) while double-JPEG rounding noise between the two codecs does not, and it is why set-re-encode-quality is observed through the DQT payloads rather than through the histogram. quantTables is excluded from the identity round trip's own comparison (ignoreKeys is not used for it; the case's handler names it), because BOTH codecs regenerate the DQT from re_encode_quality over the Annex K.1 base tables rather than carrying the source's forward.
The JPEG MARKER facts a decode-to-pixels reader destroys: the quantisation tables per index, and the JFIF APP0 version, unit and density — plus size and mode as anchors.

libjpeg's own marker walk — the ordered dump with quantisation and Huffman table rows, plus the derived table counts and the restart interval. The tool's version banner is excluded so the projection does not vary by build date.

comparisonPipelines.description: Reads two JPEG documents with an independent jpeg-jfif-codec projection (dimensions, colour type, raster digest, xmp/exif/iptc/iccProfile presence+digest) and compares them structurally. GATING for the four mutation kinds this reader can witness (`insert-other-segment`, `remove-other-segment`, `replace-pixels`, `change-re-encode-quality`); registered as a freestanding pipeline rather than wired into the existing `semantic-jpg-mutate-v1` profile's own `pipeline` field, since that profile is already the live comparison for the reclassified `image-jpeg-jfif-1-01-mutate` (`cross-semio-implementation`) oracle's own scenario (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🗿️artifacts/📷️jpg/🧪️tests/mutate-jpg-jfif-1-01/🥒️.feature`, tags `@oracle-image-jpeg-jfif-1-01-mutate @comparison-semantic-jpg-mutate-v1`) — retargeting that field would have silently redirected an existing, already-registered comparison this ticket was told to leave untouched.

A Pillow-written seed transcoded by jpegtran -restart 2. jpegtran is LOSSLESS, so the pair differs in its marker structure and not in the image — the generator asserts the Start-of-Frame line is unchanged. No library reader reaches these markers: image-rs decodes to pixels, Pillow's DRI handler is Skip and its Huffman accessors are empty and deprecated, and zune-jpeg keeps restart_interval pub(crate). djpeg -v -v prints them.

No library reader reaches these markers: image-rs decodes to pixels, Pillow's DRI handler is Skip and its Huffman accessors are empty and deprecated, and zune-jpeg keeps restart_interval pub(crate). djpeg -v -v prints them.

A Pillow-written seed encoded twice by cjpeg under 📄️four-tables.scan and 📄️three-tables.scan. The scan scripts differ by component 1's AC scan, so the table list differs by exactly one entry (AC chroma 0x11) — the generator asserts exactly one table is removed, that no new table appears, and that both halves still decode. HONEST LIMIT: the pair does NOT isolate the table from the scan. A JPEG defines a Huffman table BECAUSE a scan references it, so no conforming writer can emit a file whose table list differs by one entry while the scan list is identical; dropping the scan is the only way to drop the table. djpeg -verbose enumerates every DHT, which is what makes the table-list effect witnessable at all.
